questions.q: Which of these is an input device?
questions.explain: A keyboard sends data into the computer. The others send information out.

questions.q: Which of these is an output device?
questions.explain: A printer produces output on paper. The others put data into the computer.

questions.q: Which part of a computer is often called its 'brain'?
questions.explain: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) carries out the instructions in programs.

questions.q: What is a touchscreen?
options: Both an input and an output device
questions.explain: It displays images (output) and detects your touch (input).

questions.q: Which device would you use to record your voice?
questions.explain: A microphone captures sound and sends it into the computer.

questions.q: Which device shows a computer's display on a large wall or screen in a classroom?
questions.explain: A projector displays the computer's output on a large surface.

questions.q: What does a scanner do?
options: Turns a paper document into a digital image
questions.explain: A scanner captures paper documents or photos as digital images.

questions.q: What happens to the data in RAM when a computer is switched off?
options: It is saved to the printer
questions.explain: RAM is volatile: it needs power to keep its contents.

questions.q: Which statement about RAM and ROM is correct?
options: ROM is used to hold open programs, and RAM holds start-up instructions
RAM holds programs in use, and ROM holds start-up instructions
Both lose their data when the power is off
Neither one is a type of memory
questions.explain: RAM holds what is currently in use. ROM keeps the start-up instructions even without power.

questions.q: Which device reads the black and white lines on goods at a shop checkout?
questions.explain: A barcode reader scans the code, which identifies the product.

questions.q: What type of device is a temperature sensor in a smart air conditioner?
questions.explain: A sensor measures the surroundings and sends that data in to be processed.

questions.q: Why does a Solid State Drive (SSD) usually survive being dropped better than a Hard Disk Drive (HDD)?
questions.explain: An HDD has spinning platters and a moving arm. An SSD uses flash memory chips.

questions.q: Which is best for producing a large, highly accurate engineering drawing on paper?
questions.explain: Plotters are designed to print large, precise technical drawings.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of cache memory?
options: To keep frequently used data close to the CPU so it can be reached quickly
To connect the computer to Wi-Fi
questions.explain: Cache is small, very fast memory that speeds up the CPU's access to data.

questions.q: A smart washing machine has a small computer built in to do just one job. What is this called?
questions.explain: An embedded system is a computer built into a larger device to perform a dedicated task.

questions.q: In a greenhouse control system, which part opens the window when it gets too hot?
questions.explain: The sensor measures the temperature, and the actuator performs the physical movement.

questions.q: What does the C in CPU stand for?
questions.explain: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit.

questions.q: What device do you use to move the pointer on a desktop computer's screen? (one word)
questions.explain: A mouse controls the on-screen pointer.

questions.q: Which three-letter type of computer memory loses its contents when the power goes off?
questions.explain: RAM is volatile memory.

questions.q: What is the name for a device that measures something in its surroundings, such as light or temperature?
questions.explain: Sensors measure physical conditions and pass the data to a computer.

questions.q: Which of these is an operating system?
questions.explain: Windows manages the computer. The others are applications that run on it.

questions.q: What is software?
options: The physical parts of a computer
The programs that tell a computer what to do
questions.explain: Software is programs and instructions. Hardware is the physical equipment.

questions.q: Which program is mainly used to view websites?
questions.explain: A web browser, such as Chrome, Edge or Safari, displays web pages.

questions.q: On a computer desktop, what is a small picture that represents a program or file called?
questions.explain: An icon is a small image you can click or tap to open something.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of application software?
questions.explain: A photo editor is a program that helps a user do a task. The others are hardware.

questions.q: Android and iOS are operating systems mostly used on which devices?
questions.explain: They are the two main operating systems for mobile devices.

questions.q: What does it mean to 'install' a program?
options: To set it up on a device so that it can be used
questions.explain: Installing copies and sets up the program on your device.

questions.q: Which of these is a job of an operating system?
options: Managing files, memory and connected devices
questions.explain: The OS manages the computer's resources and lets programs run.

questions.q: What is the difference between system software and application software?
options: System software runs the computer, and application software does tasks for the user
Application software runs the computer, and system software is only for games
questions.explain: An OS is system software. A word processor is application software.

questions.q: Why should you install software updates?
options: They often fix bugs and security problems
questions.explain: Updates often repair faults and close security holes.

questions.q: What is a device driver?
options: A program that lets the operating system work with a piece of hardware
questions.explain: A driver lets the OS communicate with a device such as a printer.

questions.q: What does a 'GUI' let a user do?
options: Control a computer using windows, icons and menus
questions.explain: A Graphical User Interface uses visual items that you can point at and click.

questions.q: Which is an example of utility software?
questions.explain: Utility software helps to maintain the computer, for example by clearing unneeded files.

questions.q: What is 'open-source' software?
options: Software whose source code can be viewed and changed by others
Software that can never be updated
Software that only works without the Internet
questions.explain: The source code is publicly available, subject to the licence's terms.

questions.q: A web-based app such as Google Docs is different from installed software because it:
options: Runs through a browser, with files often stored online
Must be installed from a disc
questions.explain: Web apps run in the browser and usually keep work in cloud storage.

questions.q: How does an operating system let you appear to run several programs at once?
options: It quickly shares processor time between them
It prints each program in turn
questions.explain: This is multitasking: the OS rapidly shares CPU time between tasks.

questions.q: Are programs such as Word and Excel hardware or software?
questions.explain: They are programs, so they are software.

questions.q: What does OS stand for? (two words)
questions.explain: OS stands for Operating System.

questions.q: What three-letter short name is used for an application on a phone?
questions.explain: 'App' is short for application.

questions.q: What three-letter abbreviation means an interface that uses windows, icons and menus?
questions.explain: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface.

questions.q: How many bits make one byte?
questions.explain: One byte is made up of 8 bits.

questions.q: Which file extension is normally used for a photo?
questions.explain: .jpg is a common image format. .mp3 is audio and .xlsx is a spreadsheet.

questions.q: What is a folder used for on a computer?
questions.explain: Folders help to keep related files together.

questions.q: Which is the largest storage unit?
questions.explain: From smallest to largest: KB, MB, GB, TB.

questions.q: Which of these is a small portable storage device?
questions.explain: A USB flash drive stores files and can be carried easily.

questions.q: What does 'Save As' let you do?
options: Save the file with a new name or in a new place
questions.explain: 'Save As' makes a copy, with the name and location that you choose.

questions.q: What does 'cloud storage' mean?
options: Files stored only on your own USB drive
questions.explain: Your files are kept on remote servers and reached over the Internet.

questions.q: What is a backup?
options: A second copy of data, kept in case the original is lost
A faster version of a program
A way to make a screen brighter
questions.explain: Backups let you recover your data after a fault, deletion or attack.

questions.q: What does compressing a file do?
options: Makes the file impossible to open
questions.explain: Compression reduces file size, making it quicker to send and easier to store.

questions.q: What file type is usually best for sharing a finished document so that its layout does not change?
questions.explain: A PDF keeps its layout on most devices.

questions.q: Which file would normally take up the most storage?
questions.explain: HD video contains a huge amount of picture and sound data.

questions.q: Which is the most sensible file name for a Year 8 science project?
questions.explain: A clear name makes a file easy to identify and find later.

questions.q: Why is storing a backup somewhere separate from the original a good idea?
options: A fire or theft will not destroy both copies
questions.explain: A separate copy still survives if the original location is damaged.

questions.q: How many kilobytes are about the same as 2 megabytes?
questions.explain: 1 MB is about 1,000 KB, so 2 MB is about 2,000 KB.

questions.q: What is the difference between lossy and lossless compression?
options: Lossy permanently removes some data, and lossless keeps all of it
Lossless removes more data than lossy
Lossy is only used for text
questions.explain: JPEG photos use lossy compression. ZIP files use lossless compression.

questions.q: What does the binary number 0101 equal in ordinary (denary) numbers?
How many bits are in one byte? (type the number)
questions.explain: One byte is 8 bits.

questions.q: What three-letter file extension is often used for a photo or picture?
questions.explain: Common picture formats include JPG, PNG and GIF.

questions.q: What word means a spare copy of your data, kept in case the original is lost?
questions.explain: A backup lets you recover lost data.

questions.q: Binary uses only two digits. One is 0. What is the other?
questions.explain: Binary uses only 0 and 1.

questions.q: Which program is best for typing a letter?
questions.explain: Word processors, such as Microsoft Word, are designed for text documents.

questions.q: Which program is designed for creating a slide show?
questions.explain: PowerPoint and Google Slides are presentation programs.

questions.q: What does the Bold button do to selected text?
options: Moves it to a new page
questions.explain: Bold makes text stand out by making it thicker.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut normally copies selected text on Windows?
questions.explain: Ctrl + C copies. Ctrl + V pastes.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut normally undoes your last action on Windows?
questions.explain: Ctrl + Z is Undo.

questions.q: What does a spell checker do?
questions.explain: It highlights words that may be spelt incorrectly.

questions.q: In a presentation, what is each single page called?
questions.explain: A presentation is made up of a series of slides.

questions.q: What is a good rule for text on a presentation slide?
options: Fill the slide with long paragraphs
Keep it short with clear key points
Use a different font in each line
questions.explain: Short points are easy to read while the speaker explains the details.

questions.q: Where should you put a page number so that it repeats on every page of a document?
questions.explain: Headers and footers repeat at the top and bottom of each page.

questions.q: Which text alignment lines text up neatly along both the left and right margins?
questions.explain: Justified text adjusts the spacing so that both edges are even.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'Cut' and 'Copy'?
options: Cut removes the original, and Copy leaves it in place
Copy removes the original, and Cut leaves it in place
questions.explain: Both place the item on the clipboard, but Cut also removes the original.

questions.q: Which colour choice is easiest to read on a projected slide?
questions.explain: High contrast between text and background makes reading easy.

questions.q: What is the effect of a slide 'transition'?
options: It controls how one slide changes to the next
It adds a page number to a letter
questions.explain: A transition is the visual effect shown when moving between slides.

questions.q: Why use built-in heading styles in a long document?
options: They make the file impossible to edit
They let you format consistently and create an automatic contents page
questions.explain: Styles keep formatting consistent, and tables of contents are generated from headings.

questions.q: What does 'mail merge' do?
options: Combines one letter with a list of data to make personalised copies
questions.explain: It fills in fields such as names and addresses, creating a personalised copy for each person.

questions.q: When you stretch a photo by dragging only one side, what is the likely result?
options: The photo looks distorted because its aspect ratio changed
questions.explain: Changing width and height unevenly alters the aspect ratio and distorts the image.

questions.q: In a presentation program, what do we call one page of the show?
questions.explain: A presentation is a series of slides.

questions.q: Which letter is used with Ctrl to paste on Windows?
questions.explain: Ctrl + V pastes.

questions.q: What is the area at the bottom of each page of a document called, where page numbers often go?
questions.explain: The footer repeats at the bottom of each page.

questions.q: What two-word feature makes personalised letters from one template and a list of names?
questions.explain: Mail merge combines a document with a data source.

questions.q: Which program is a spreadsheet?
questions.explain: Excel and Google Sheets are spreadsheet programs.

questions.q: In a spreadsheet, what is one box in the grid called?
questions.explain: Each box where a column and row meet is a cell.

questions.q: What is the cell reference for column B, row 3?
questions.explain: A cell reference gives the column letter and then the row number.

questions.q: Which symbol must a spreadsheet formula start with?
questions.explain: Formulas begin with an equals sign.

questions.q: How are the columns in a spreadsheet usually labelled?
questions.explain: Columns use letters (A, B, C) and rows use numbers.

questions.q: Which function adds up a group of numbers?
questions.explain: SUM adds the values in a range.

questions.q: Which symbol is used for multiplication in a spreadsheet formula?
questions.explain: Spreadsheets use * for multiplication, as in =A1*B1.

questions.q: Which formula works out the average of cells A1 to A5?
questions.explain: AVERAGE adds the values and divides by how many there are.

questions.q: Which function finds the highest score in a list?
questions.explain: MAX returns the largest value in the range.

questions.q: A1 contains 4 and B1 contains 5. What does =A1*B1 show?
What happens to a formula's result if you change a number that it uses?
questions.explain: Automatic recalculation is one of the main benefits of spreadsheets.

questions.q: Which chart is best for showing how each subject's share makes up a whole timetable?
questions.explain: Pie charts show parts of a whole.

questions.q: What does a cell showing ##### usually mean?
options: The column is too narrow to display the value
questions.explain: Widening the column normally lets the value be displayed.

questions.q: What does the $ do in the cell reference $A$1?
options: Keeps the reference fixed when the formula is copied
questions.explain: This is an absolute reference. It does not change when copied to other cells.

questions.q: What result does =IF(A1>=50,"Pass","Fail") give when A1 contains 50?
questions.explain: 50 is greater than or equal to 50, so the condition is true and it returns Pass.

questions.q: The formula =A1+B1 in cell C1 is copied down to C2. What does it become?
questions.explain: Relative references change to match the new row.

questions.q: Which function name adds a range of numbers? (three letters)
questions.explain: SUM adds up values.

questions.q: What is one box in a spreadsheet grid called?
questions.explain: Each box is a cell.

questions.q: Which function name finds the smallest value in a range? (three letters)
questions.explain: MIN returns the lowest value.

questions.q: A1 is 10 and A2 is 6. What number does =A1-A2*0 show?
questions.explain: Multiplication comes first: 6 × 0 = 0, and 10 − 0 = 10.

questions.q: What is a database?
questions.explain: Databases organise data so that it can be stored, searched and updated.

questions.q: A school keeps details of its students in a table. What is all the information about one student called?
questions.explain: A record holds all the data about one person or thing.

questions.q: In a student table, what is 'Date of Birth' an example of?
questions.explain: A field holds one category of information.

questions.q: Which of these would most likely use a database?
questions.explain: A library system needs to store and search for details of books and borrowers.

questions.q: What does it mean to 'sort' data?
questions.explain: Sorting arranges data, for example from A to Z or highest to lowest.

questions.q: Which data type is best for storing a student's name?
questions.explain: Names are made of letters, so they are stored as text.

questions.q: Which data type is best for storing whether a library book is on loan?
questions.explain: Only two values are possible, so a Yes/No type fits.

questions.q: What is a query used for in a database?
options: To find the data that matches certain criteria
questions.explain: A query asks the database for matching records.

questions.q: Why does a student table use a Student ID as its key field?
options: Each student's ID is unique, unlike names
questions.explain: A primary key uniquely identifies each record. Two students could have the same name.

questions.q: What does a filter do?
options: Shows only the records that match a condition
questions.explain: A filter hides records that do not match, without deleting them.

questions.q: Which data type is best for a phone number such as 0123456?
options: Number, so that it can be added up
Text, so that the leading zero is kept
questions.explain: A phone number is not used in calculations, and text keeps the leading zero.

questions.q: What does data validation do?
options: Checks that entered data is sensible and follows rules
questions.explain: Validation checks entered data, for example that an age is within a range. It cannot prove that it is true.

questions.q: Which validation check would reject the age 150 for a Year 7 student?
questions.explain: A range check makes sure that a value lies between limits.

questions.q: What is the difference between validation and verification?
options: Validation checks data is reasonable, and verification checks it was entered correctly from its source
Verification deletes data, and validation prints it
questions.explain: Double entry is an example of verification. A range check is validation.

questions.q: Why link two tables, such as Students and Classes, instead of repeating class details in every student's record?
options: To reduce repeated data and errors
To make the data slower to search
questions.explain: A relational design stores each fact once, so updates stay consistent.

questions.q: Which criteria finds students who are in Year 9 and scored over 80?
questions.explain: AND needs both conditions to be true.

questions.q: What word means all the data about one person or thing in a database table?
questions.explain: A record is one complete entry.

questions.q: What is one category of data in a table, such as 'Surname', called?
questions.explain: A field is shown as a column in a table.

questions.q: What is a request to find particular data in a database called?
questions.explain: A query searches a database for matching data.

questions.q: What two-word term means the field that uniquely identifies each record?
questions.explain: A primary key (or key field) must be unique for each record.

questions.q: What is a computer network?
options: Computers connected to share data and resources
A single computer that is switched off
questions.explain: Networks let devices communicate and share things such as files and printers.

questions.q: What does 'www' stand for in a web address?
questions.explain: www stands for World Wide Web.

questions.q: What does Wi-Fi let a laptop do?
options: Connect to a network without a cable
questions.explain: Wi-Fi is a wireless connection to a network.

questions.q: What is a search engine used for?
questions.explain: Google and Bing are examples of search engines.

questions.q: What does it mean to 'download' a file?
options: To copy it from the Internet to your device
To copy it from your device to a website
questions.explain: Downloading brings data to your device. Uploading sends it away.

questions.q: What does a URL identify?
options: The address of a web page
questions.explain: A URL is a web address, such as https://www.example.com.

questions.q: Which symbol is always found in an email address?
questions.explain: The @ symbol separates the user's name from the domain.

questions.q: What is the difference between a LAN and a WAN?
options: A LAN covers a small area, and a WAN covers a large area
A LAN can never share files
questions.explain: A school network is a LAN. The Internet is the largest example of a WAN.

questions.q: What does a router do?
options: Directs data between networks, such as a home network and the Internet
Stores all of your photos forever
questions.explain: A router sends data packets towards their destinations.

questions.q: What does the padlock or 'https' in a browser's address bar usually show?
options: The website can never contain scams
questions.explain: HTTPS encrypts the connection, but it does not prove that a site can be trusted.

questions.q: What is bandwidth?
options: The width of a network cable
How much data can be transferred per second
The number of websites you own
questions.explain: Higher bandwidth means that more data can be sent in the same time.

questions.q: What is the difference between the Internet and the World Wide Web?
options: The Internet is the global network, and the Web is pages accessed over it
The Web is the cables, and the Internet is web pages
The Internet works only on phones
questions.explain: The Web is one service that runs on the Internet. Email is another.

questions.q: What does 'CC' mean when sending an email?
options: Sends a copy to another person
questions.explain: CC stands for carbon copy. Everyone can see who was copied.

questions.q: What does DNS do?
options: Translates website names into IP addresses
questions.explain: DNS works like a phone book, finding the IP address for a domain name.

questions.q: How is data sent across the Internet?
options: Split into packets, which are reassembled at the destination
questions.explain: Packets can take different routes and are put back in order on arrival.

questions.q: Why are fibre-optic cables better than copper cables for long distances?
options: They carry light signals with less signal loss and higher speeds
They need no equipment at either end
questions.explain: Light pulses in glass fibres travel far, with little loss and high bandwidth.

questions.q: What word means copying a file from the Internet to your device?
questions.explain: Downloading brings data to your device.

questions.q: What program do you use to open web pages? (type the general name)
questions.explain: A web browser displays web pages.

questions.q: What three-letter abbreviation means a network in a small area, such as a school?
questions.explain: LAN stands for Local Area Network.

questions.q: What small pieces is data split into when it is sent across the Internet?
questions.explain: Data is sent as packets.

questions.q: Which of these is the strongest password?
questions.explain: Strong passwords are long, hard to guess and mix character types.

questions.q: What should you do if a stranger online asks for your home address?
options: Do not share it, and tell a trusted adult
Send them your password as well
questions.explain: Keep personal information private, and report concerns.

questions.q: What is cyberbullying?
options: Using technology to repeatedly hurt or embarrass someone
questions.explain: It includes hurtful messages and posts, or shaming someone online.

questions.q: Should you share your school account password with a friend?
options: Yes, but only in a group chat
questions.explain: Anyone who has your password can act as you.

questions.q: What is a computer virus?
options: A harmful program that can damage files or spread
An illness caught from a keyboard
questions.explain: A virus is one type of malicious software, or malware.

questions.q: An email says you won a prize and asks you to click a link. What should you do?
options: Be suspicious and do not click
questions.explain: This is a common scam used to steal information.

questions.q: What should you do when you finish using a shared school computer?
options: Write your password on the desk
Share your login with the next person
questions.explain: Logging out stops others from using your account.

questions.q: What is phishing?
options: Fake messages designed to trick people into giving personal details
A way of speeding up Wi-Fi
questions.explain: Phishing messages pretend to be from a trusted source.

questions.q: What is a 'digital footprint'?
options: The record of what you do and share online
questions.explain: Posts, searches and accounts can leave lasting traces.

questions.q: What does copyright protect?
options: Creators' rights over their original work
questions.explain: You generally need permission to copy or reuse protected work.

questions.q: What is plagiarism?
options: Presenting someone else's work as your own
questions.explain: Avoid it by using your own words and crediting your sources.

questions.q: What does two-factor authentication (2FA) add to logging in?
options: A second way of proving who you are, such as a code on your phone
questions.explain: Even if a password is stolen, the attacker still needs the second factor.

questions.q: Which is a good way to check whether information found online is reliable?
options: Believe it if it has many likes
Compare it with other trusted sources
Check only that the page looks attractive
questions.explain: Check the author, the date and whether other reliable sources agree.

questions.q: What does ransomware do?
options: Locks or encrypts files and demands payment
questions.explain: Good backups reduce the harm that a ransomware attack can cause.

questions.q: What is the role of a firewall?
options: Monitoring network traffic and blocking unauthorised access
questions.explain: A firewall applies rules to control what can pass in and out of a network.

questions.q: Why is public Wi-Fi riskier for logging in to online banking?
options: Others on the network may be able to intercept unprotected data
Banks do not work on Wi-Fi
It uses up your phone's memory
questions.explain: Open networks can be monitored or faked, so avoid sensitive activities on them.

questions.q: What secret word or phrase protects your online account?
questions.explain: Keep passwords strong and private.

questions.q: What word means bullying someone using technology?
questions.explain: Save the evidence and tell a trusted adult.

questions.q: What word means tricking someone with fake messages to steal their details?
questions.explain: Phishing messages pretend to be from trusted sources.

questions.q: What word means general malicious software, including viruses and spyware?
questions.explain: Malware is short for malicious software.
